title: Hof operation journal (v2, kind-generic)
description: /var/lib/hof/state/journal/<operationId>.json - the durable, per-operation-run header record on the target. Identical to operation-journal-v1 except for the added operationKind field (ADR 0006) and its own committedGeneration semantics below. Written once at operation start (immutable except `status`/`committedGeneration`, updated only by the same operationId that created it); individual attempts are recorded separately as an append-only operation-event-v1 log (unchanged, kind-agnostic) this journal's own operationId ties them to. A pre-existing journal written before this ADR has no operationKind field and does not validate against this schema - an executor must still read and safely resume it as operation-journal-v1 (implicit "apply"), never refuse it outright just because the field is absent. Never holds a secret value, decrypted content, an environment dump, or an SSH private-key path - safe to read, copy, or attach to a bug report without a second sanitization pass.

operationKind.description: Which of the three operation state machines produced this journal. Decides which plan schema `plan` below was validated against before being embedded (plan-v2 for apply, backup-plan-v1 for backup, restore-plan-v1 for restore) and this journal's own committedGeneration semantics (see below).

approvedPlanId.description: The exact plan this run was approved against (--approve-plan-id) - equal to plan.planId below by construction, regardless of operationKind.

plan.description: The full, exact plan document this operation was approved against - not just its planId. Loosely typed here on purpose (no schema in this repo cross-references another by $id) - already validated against the schema matching operationKind before ever being embedded.

inputDigests.description: Every input this specific run is bound to, fixed at journal creation and never recomputed from a live file again mid-run. executionEnvironmentDigest is the EE image actually dispatched from - for backup/restore this is the backup-tool-lock's own pinned image, not necessarily the platform release's ansibleEnvironment image (ADR 0006's whole point: a backup/restore tool build moves independently of the platform release).

status.description: in-progress: the operation is running or was interrupted and not yet resolved either way. succeeded: every dispatched operation completed (for backup, every configured destination - a partial result is a failure here, recorded separately in backup-evidence-v1). failed: a fatal, unresumable outcome - the operator must diagnose per this operationKind's own recovery rules, never blindly retry this same journal.

committedGeneration.description: apply: the newly-committed generation once state.commit succeeds, exactly as operation-journal-v1. backup: always null, even on success - a backup never mutates current.json or the generation at all. restore: the restored SOURCE generation once state.restore succeeds, carried forward verbatim, never incremented - this is the same installation's history continuing on new hardware, not a new applied change. Null for the entire lifetime of a run that never reaches its own commit point, including every failed one, regardless of kind.

allOf.description: The status/committedGeneration/operationKind pairing this schema's own field descriptions above already document, actually enforced - reusing operation-journal-v1's own already-reviewed if/then/else mechanism (2026-08-31), extended one level for operationKind's own backup exception.
